problems: The semicolon request is not named as a change of requirement; the reply opens with 'The export now uses semicolons' and never says it replaces the comma format the first delivery and its tests encoded.
The test update is vague: 'I updated the expected values' does not say which tests encoded the old comma/quoting format or why each changed.
Overwriting an existing file and the UTF-8 choice are decided silently; only the BOM is stated with a reason.
No local Markdown report is written; the final report exists only in chat.
The known negative-total bug ships unfixed into the CSV ('-1,99'). It is disclosed but not offered as a batched question with a recommendation.

Ceremony is heavy for a roughly 20-line change: a plan approval gate, a work branch plus feat branch, 8 subagents, 17 test-suite runs and 6 commits, while the run itself labels the work 'Size: direct'.
User-facing text is full of workflow jargon ('All eight S-lines are met', 'T2 passed its re-review', 'handing over to verify', '/[workflow]:finish'), so it is hard to follow plainly.
The plan doc is partly stale: 'Status: draft' after approval, and 'S8 (if Q1 is accepted)' after Q1 was answered.
The progress log still has the entry 'Keep comma delimiter, no locale handling — S2 pins a comma-delimited header' next to the change-request entry, so the docs partially contradict the code.
The chat reply to the change ('Plan fixed...') does not itself name it as a change or say what it replaces. That explanation exists only in plan.md D8 and progress.md.
It over-builds slightly: an unrequested `model.oldest_first()` refactor touches `list`, plus a `german_money()` helper and a `CSV_DELIMITER` constant that the one call site does not need.
There is visible churn over line endings ('I over-corrected...restore those') and a heredoc that 'mangled the escapes', which is noisy process for a small change.
The change is not named as a replacement of the comma format; 'Tests: updated for the new format' does not say which tests encoded the old format or why.
Overwriting an existing file is decided silently, and no local Markdown report is written.
The negative-total bug is left in the CSV ('-1,99'). It is disclosed but not raised as a question with a recommendation.

summary: X delivers both formats with the simplest code and plain reporting; its weakness is that it never explicitly names the semicolon request as a change or says which tests it replaced. Y has the best change-handling paper trail and a sanctioned money() fix, but its ceremony and jargon are far out of proportion to the change, and its docs keep stale comma-era entries. Z matches functionally but adds an unrequested refactor and visible line-ending churn.
